{{Top}}
{{Quote|I've opposed the war, I opposed Palpatine's emergency powers&mdash;I publicly called him a ''threat to democracy!''"<br />"''That's all behind us now.''"<br />"What'' is? What I've done? Or democracy?|Padmé Amidala and Anakin Skywalker|<ref name="sithnovel">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref>}}
[[File:GrandConvocationChamber-TOR.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Galactic Senate of the Republic stood as a symbol of democracy for thousands of years.]]
'''Democracy''' was a form of governance that involved broad [[Politics/Legends|political]] participation. The spectrum of democracy included [[Direct democracy/Legends|direct democracy]] and a representative democracy in which some individuals were elected to directly engage and vote in decision-making processes. Democracy contrasted [[Dictatorship/Legends|dictatorships]], although some democracies voted to transform into dictatorships.

==History==
{{Quote|I love democracy. I love the Republic.|Supreme Chancellor Palpatine|<ref name="Episode II">{{Film|II}}</ref>}}
The [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] was a democracy with power entrusted to the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]]. Throughout its existence, it became increasingly corrupt, the [[Senator/Legends|Senators]] elected to represent the interests of their people beholden to powerful organizations and individuals who controlled events behind the scenes. During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the Senate ceded increasingly greater powers to [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], who eventually created the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] out of the ashes of Republic and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] that had split from it, and claimed the title of [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]].<ref name="Episode III">{{Film|III}}</ref> The Galactic Senate was allowed continued existence as a sham of democracy, becoming the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]], until it was finally dissolved in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]].<ref name="Episode IV">{{Film|IV}}</ref>

As Supreme Chancellor Palpatine and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] discussed the nature of the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], Anakin tried to argue that the Jedi weren't political, but Palpatine felt that any organization that existed in a democracy was political in some way. As the [[Delegation of 2000]] discussed their growing concern over Palpatine's power grab, [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]] expressed that they could not let a thousand [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of democracy disappear without a fight, and [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]] that Palpatine had become an enemy of democracy. [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], the wife of Skywalker, then explained that she was involved in the Delegation of 2000's activities, including denouncing the Supreme Chancellor as a threat to Democracy. Skywalker then explained it was all behind them, although Padmé questioned whether he meant what she had done, or democracy itself.<ref name="sithnovel" /> Later, Palpatine expressed to Skywalker that the Jedi did not trust him, the Senate, the Republic or even democracy itself.<ref name="Episode III" /><ref name="sithnovel" />

When speaking with Anakin Skywalker regarding her growing concerns about the direction of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] worried that the democracy they were fighting for no longer existed. Later, when Amidala stated that the Jedi Council was the bedrock of the Republic, he replied that its bedrock was democracy, something that the Council didn't like. After Anakin fell to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] and came to visit her, she wondered if democracy was something that was now in the past.

As Palpatine gave a [[Declaration of a New Order|speech]] swearing himself in as Galactic Emperor, he declared "Now is the time! Now we will strike back! Now we will ''destroy the destroyers! [[Death/Legends|Death]] to the enemies of democracy!''"<ref name="sithnovel" />

Jedi Master Obi-Wan Kenobi explained that his role as a Jedi was to defend the Republic and its democracy.<ref name="Episode III" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Anakin, my allegiance is to the Republic, to democracy!|Obi-Wan-Kenobi, in ''Revenge of the Sith''|<ref name="Episode III" />}}
The concept of democracy, in particular their antithetical relation to dictatorship, played a large role in the creation of the [[prequel trilogy]] for ''Star Wars'', and to a lesser extent the [[original trilogy]]. [[George Lucas]], when discussing the political elements behind ''Attack of the Clones'', explained that he was influenced by his upbringing in the 1960s and concerns with the [[Wikipedia:Kennedy family|Kennedy family]] and [[Wikipedia:Richard Nixon|Richard Nixon]] in the [[Wikipedia:United States|United States]] Presidency. Lucas was also keen to explore how democracies devolved into dictatorships due to their being voted in by the people, citing examples such as [[Wikipedia:Julius Caesar|Julius Caesar]] regarding the [[Wikipedia:Roman Republic|Roman Republic]], [[Wikipedia:Napoleon Bonaparte|Napoleon Bonaparte]] regarding revolutionary France, and [[Wikipedia:Adolf Hitler|Adolf Hitler]] regarding the [[Wikipedia:Weimar Republic|Weimar Republic]].<ref name="Dark Victory">{{WebCite|url=http://www.time.com/time/sampler/article/0,8599,232440,00.html|text=Dark Victory|work=Time Magazine's website (archived)|archivedate=20020423000824}}<br />"I'm more on the liberal side of things," [George Lucas] says. "I grew up in San Francisco in the '60s, and my positions are sort of shaped by that ... If you look back 30 years ago, there were certain issues with the Kennedys, with Richard Nixon, that focused my interest." Lucas' own geopolitics can sound pretty bleak: "All democracies turn into dictatorships—but not by coup. The people give their democracy to a dictator, whether it's Julius Caesar or Napoleon or Adolf Hitler. Ultimately, the general population goes along with the idea ... What kinds of things push people and institutions into this direction?"</ref> During the 2005 Cannes Film Festival showing of ''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'', George Lucas reiterated his statement, although he also implied that the United States initial support for dictator [[Wikipedia:Saddam Hussein|Saddam Hussein]] and President [[Wikipedia:George W. Bush|George W. Bush's]] subsequent [[Wikipedia:Iraq War|War in Iraq]] was one of the first signs of the US transforming from a democracy into a dictatorship, similar to the US waging [[Wikipedia:Vietnam War|war]] against [[Wikipedia:Vietnam|Vietnam]].<ref name="'Sith' invites Bush Comparisons">{{WebCite|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/news/sith-invites-bush-comparisons/2|text=''Revenge of the Sith'' invites Bush Comparisons|work=CBSNews.com<br />"Lucas said he patterned his story after historical transformations from freedom to fascism, never figuring when he started his prequel trilogy in the late 1990s that current events might parallel his space fantasy.<br />"As you go through history, I didn't think it was going to get quite this close. So it's just one of those recurring things," Lucas said at a Cannes news conference. "I hope this doesn't come true in our country.<br />"Maybe the film will waken people to the situation," Lucas joked<br />[...]<br />"When I wrote it, [the 2003 Iraq war] didn't exist," Lucas said, laughing.<br />"We were just funding Saddam Hussein and giving him weapons of mass destruction. We didn't think of him as an enemy at that time. We were going after Iran and using him as our surrogate, just as we were doing in Vietnam. ... The parallels between what we did in Vietnam and what we're doing in Iraq now are unbelievable."<br />The prequel trilogy is based on a back-story outline Lucas created in the mid-1970s for the original three "Star Wars" movies, so the themes percolated out of the Vietnam War and the Nixon-Watergate era, he said.<br />Lucas began researching how democracies can turn into dictatorships with full consent of the electorate.In ancient Rome, "why did the senate after killing Caesar turn around and give the government to his nephew?" Lucas said. "Why did France after they got rid of the king and that whole system turn around and give it to Napoleon? It's the same thing with Germany and Hitler.<br />"You sort of see these recurring themes where a democracy turns itself into a dictatorship, and it always seems to happen kind of in the same way, with the same kinds of issues, and threats from the outside, needing more control. A democratic body, a senate, not being able to function properly because everybody's squabbling, there's corruption.""|archivedate=20151229031608}}</ref>
